notes: BAS_* entries jump to the BASIC routine named by target. They work only while BASIC is in memory, not in a program that has loaded over it.

entries.description: Reset entry (MIA points RESET here): sets up the machine and the console, prints the banner and starts BASIC.
Re-enters BASIC at READY, keeping the program and variables; resets the stack, IRQ_VEC, bank 0 and the VIA (every interrupt source off but Timer 1, which restarts at 6250) first.
Writes the character in A to the console at the cursor, handling control codes; A, X and Y are preserved.
Waits for one key from MIA's input FIFO and returns it in A, showing the cursor meanwhile.
Returns C=1 and the next key in A if one is waiting, else C=0, without waiting.
Clears the overlay text screen and homes the cursor.
Prints the low nibble of A as one hex digit.
Prints A as two hex digits.
Prints the zero-terminated string KPTR points at, up to 255 bytes.
Streams a PRG file into CPU RAM. A is the bank for $8000-$BFFF and KPTR a destination override or 0; C=1 jumps to KTMP (0 for the first byte) instead of returning.
Screen editor: returns the next character of the line edited on screen, ending with CR; BASIC reads its input lines through it.
Draws A as a raw glyph at the cursor, never as a control code; A, X and Y are preserved.
Enters the WozMon monitor; its Q command returns to BASIC through KERN_WARMSTART.
Sets the screen backdrop color selector to A.
The kernel's IRQ handler: a program's own handler restores A, X and Y and ends with JMP KERN_IRQ.
C=1 reads the cursor into X (row) and Y (column); C=0 moves it there and returns C=1 if that is off the screen.
Copies MIA's clock into CLOCK_SNAPSHOT ($02F8-$02FF); returns C=1 if the firmware has a clock.
Sets MIA's 60 Hz count, BASIC's TI, from A, X and Y, low byte first.
Skips the comma at TXTPTR, else raises SYNTAX ERROR; A is the next character.
Evaluates the numeric expression at TXTPTR into FAC; a string raises TYPE MISMATCH.
Evaluates any expression at TXTPTR into FAC; VALTYP is $FF for a string, whose descriptor address is then in FAC+3 and FAC+4.
Converts FAC to a 16-bit value in LINNUM, A (high) and Y (low); outside 0-65535 raises ILLEGAL QUANTITY.
Evaluates the numeric expression at TXTPTR into X; outside 0-255 raises ILLEGAL QUANTITY.
Finds or creates the variable named at TXTPTR and returns its value's address in VARPNT, A (low) and Y (high).
Raises the BASIC error whose code is in X (basic.json errors): maps bank 0, prints it and returns to READY.
Prints A (high) and X (low) as an unsigned decimal, with PRINT's leading space.
